planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring or fall; this slow-growing sport is a bit fussier to establish than other transatlantica daphnes and benefits from being left undisturbed once sited.

directions: Moon Canyon arose as a branch mutation on 'Summer Ice' and carries the same rounded habit but with broader, more pronounced cream-to-yellow leaf margins framing a green center. Soft pink buds open to pure white, intensely perfumed flowers in a heavy spring flush with lighter repeat bloom into summer. Site it in well-drained soil with afternoon shade in hot climates, since variegated foliage scorches faster than solid green daphnes in strong sun. Growth is noticeably slower than other burkwood and transatlantica hybrids, so expect it to take longer to fill in and avoid heavy pruning while it establishes.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in a sheltered, partly shaded bed; like other winter daphnes it resents root disturbance once established.

directions: Banana Split is a variegated sport of winter daphne with a wide, clean yellow margin wrapping each glossy green leaf, giving the whole shrub a brighter look than plain-leaved odora selections. Clusters of rose-pink buds open through late winter into sweetly fragrant, nearly white flowers at the branch tips. Grow it in humus-rich, well-drained soil with protection from harsh winter wind and afternoon sun, the same conditions that suit other Daphne odora cultivars. Keep an eye out for reversion shoots with plain green leaves and prune these out to keep the variegation strong.

planting.note: Plant in spring into gritty, fast-draining soil; this rock-garden hybrid dislikes winter wet at the crown more than most daphnes.

directions: A hybrid between D. cneorum and D. collina raised by British daphne breeder Robin White, Meon forms a low, bushy mound of dark green leaves noticeably larger than those of either parent. Deep pink buds open to fragrant, paler pink flowers in unusually large clusters for a dwarf daphne, with a reliable rebloom later in the season. It wants a sunny, gritty, sharply drained site, ideally a raised bed or rock garden, where its roots stay dry through winter. Avoid rich, moisture-retentive soil, which shortens the life of most dwarf alpine daphnes including this one.

planting.note: Plant in spring in lean, gravelly, well-drained soil in full sun; this Mediterranean species wants its wood baked by summer heat to flower and overwinter well.

directions: Native to rocky hillsides around the Mediterranean from Italy to Crete and Asia Minor, silky daphne forms a dense, upright evergreen mound topped in mid-spring with clusters of intensely fragrant, deep rose-pink flowers. It is one of the two parents of the popular Daphne x transatlantica hybrids and shares their heat tolerance, doing best with full sun and dry, gravelly, lime-tolerant soil rather than the cool, moist shade preferred by Daphne odora. Established plants are quite drought tolerant and resent heavy, wet winter soil far more than they mind summer dryness. Give it room to form its naturally dense, rounded shape without crowding from taller shrubs.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in well-drained soil; tolerates sun to fairly deep shade, making it a flexible screen or hedge plant for mixed-light borders.

directions: Despite its name, Fastigiata is not a true columnar form but grows into a dense, rounded holly-leaved shrub, looser and quicker to fill in than many other heterophyllus cultivars. Young leaves carry the spiny, holly-like teeth typical of the species but smooth out to simple entire margins as the plant matures. Tiny cream flowers tucked in the leaf axils open in fall and carry a heady, carnation-like fragrance well beyond the shrub itself. It handles light shade better than most fragrant shrubs and makes a reliable unclipped screen or informal hedge once established.

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in acidic, well-drained soil; its large eventual size and pyramidal habit make it best suited to screening or specimen use rather than a small foundation planting.

directions: Patty's Secret grows into a dense, pyramidal large shrub or small tree with glossy, dark green leaves that stay handsome year-round. Clusters of small white flowers tucked among the foliage open in fall and release a sweet fragrance that carries well beyond the plant on cool evenings. It tolerates heat, drought, and a range of soil conditions once established, and its size and density make it one of the better broadleaf evergreens for a tall, year-round privacy screen. Give it full sun to light shade and room to reach its mature height without regular hard pruning, since flowering is reduced on plants sheared heavily every year.
